summary: Closes the openbao-finalizer/ESO-adoption race by introducing a Pass-0 adoption gate in finalizeOpenBaoSecrets. Before the existing Delete loop (Pass-1) fires, the finalizer now inspects each backup PushSecret and, if any still lacks the ESO cleanup finalizer 'pushsecret.externalsecrets.external-secrets.io/finalizer', returns early with a SecretsReady=False / Reason=WaitingForESOAdoption condition. Once every live PushSecret carries the ESO finalizer (or is already Terminating or absent), the existing Delete then wait-for-gone logic runs unchanged. Symmetric helpers (hasESOFinalizer, setOpenBaoWaitingForESOAdoptionCondition) mirror the existing OpenBaoFinalizerBlocked shape. Unit coverage adds 9 tests including an RBAC-shape interceptor test asserting only get+delete verbs are exercised, an envtest integration test (TestIntegrationKeystone_DeleteRacingESOAdoption) reproduces the original race end-to-end, and the deletion-cleanup chainsaw step-6 now retries bao kv get for up to 30s. No RBAC, helm, or CRD changes; no new external dependencies. go vet, go build, and golangci-lint --new-from-rev=main are clean; all 16 targeted unit tests pass under -race.

tests_checklist.item: Unit tests cover the new Pass-0 adoption gate (blocks / proceeds / mixed / terminating / absent)
RBAC-shape test asserts only get+delete verbs touch PushSecrets (interceptor.Funcs over all 7 verbs)
Pin test guards the ESO finalizer string constant against drift
Envtest integration test reproduces the Delete-before-adoption race and asserts Pass-0 block -> ESO adoption -> teardown
Existing TestFinalizeOpenBaoSecrets_DeletesBothPushSecrets and TestIntegration_OpenBaoFinalizerLifecycle_AddAndRemove still pass with adjusted fixtures
Chainsaw deletion-cleanup step-6 retry loop preserves ERROR messaging and non-zero exit on timeout
Tests use Gomega NewGomegaWithT(t) per project convention

code_quality_checklist.item: Pass-0 helper functions small and focused (hasESOFinalizer, setOpenBaoWaitingForESOAdoptionCondition)
Naming mirrors existing OpenBaoFinalizerBlocked shape for symmetry
ESO finalizer string defined as a single package constant (esoPushSecretFinalizer)
Function doc-comment updated from 2-pass to 3-pass with CC-0091/REQ-001/REQ-003 references
No dead code, no commented-out code, no magic strings
golangci-lint --new-from-rev=main reports zero issues on changed code

security_checklist.item: Pass-0 gate prevents Delete on unadopted PushSecrets, preventing leaked Fernet/credential keys in OpenBao KV-v2 (primary goal)
Condition messages use %q formatting for user-controlled names (no format-string injection)
No new attack surface: reads finalizer list, writes condition, no new API verbs required
No secrets logged; condition message names the PushSecret only

architecture_checklist.item: Two Reasons on SecretsReady=False are mutually exclusive: WaitingForESOAdoption (pre-Delete) vs OpenBaoFinalizerBlocked (post-Delete)
RBAC surface unchanged: existing get;list;watch;create;update;patch;delete on pushsecrets covers the new read path
No CRD schema, helm chart, or config/rbac/ changes
Pass-0 is additive and idempotent: absent and Terminating PushSecrets short-circuit cleanly
Docs updated (keystone-reconciler.md): two-stage lifecycle table, WaitingForESOAdoption condition reference

dry_yagni_checklist.item: Uses existing conditions.SetCondition helper; no new condition infrastructure
ESO finalizer string is a single constant; test references it via the exported symbol rather than duplicating the literal
No speculative abstractions (e.g., no generic 'adoption gate' framework)
Pin test is a deliberate drift-protection probe, not duplication

fail_fast_checklist.item: Pass-0 returns early with a clear requeue-eligible condition when any PushSecret is unadopted
Absent PushSecret is treated as 'nothing to protect' (IsNotFound tolerated, loop continues)
Terminating PushSecret treated as adopted (DeletionTimestamp != nil) to avoid deadlock on concurrent deletion

defensive_checklist.item: Condition message truncation not needed (single PushSecret name)
ObservedGeneration plumbed through so stale conditions are detectable

suggested_improvements: Optional nit: the two SecretsReady=False reasons use slightly asymmetric message phrasing ('waiting for ESO to adopt %q' vs 'PushSecret %q still present after Delete'). Aligning phrasing around a common 'PushSecret %q: <state>' template would make logs easier to scan, but this is stylistic only.
Optional nit: consider exporting esoPushSecretFinalizer (as ESOPushSecretFinalizer) if another controller in this module ever needs to reason about the same string; not required for CC-0091.
next_steps: Merge as-is; no blocking or major issues were identified.
If e2e flakes resurface around step-6 despite the 30s retry, revisit OpenBao propagation latency rather than extending the chainsaw window further.
